## This week

The slides start from one question: an agent calls the model many times for one task, so what should the model see at each call? Part 1 defines the context and the trajectory, shows three ways a context makes the output worse (length: context rot; position: lost in the middle; content: context failures), and defines context engineering with its four strategies. Part 2 writes information outside the context: a scratchpad within a task, long-term memory across tasks, and memory updates. Part 3 selects what goes in: just-in-time retrieval, tool selection, memory retrieval, and the order of the parts. Part 4 compresses the context: tool-result clearing, trimming, compaction, and prompt compression. Part 5 isolates work in sub-agents and shows when that fits.

## Practice and lab

Practice 1 (above) is to be done before class. It introduces LangChain: a model call with `invoke` and message objects, structured output, tools with `@tool`, and an agent with `create_agent` that continues a conversation in a thread; it ends with exercises. Practice 2 turns the RAG program of Week 9 into agentic RAG: the retriever becomes a tool, and the model decides when and how to search. The agent answers a greeting without a search, searches again when a first result is not enough, stops at `recursion_limit`, and keeps a thread for a follow-up question. The lab is the program of Practice 2 with five blocks for you to write between `FILL IN` lines; a check cell follows each block, and the last cell prints LAB COMPLETE when all checks pass.
